input: one thing I want to do is look at the development of religion through heavy research and synthesis. lots of citations etc. / maybe a blog series ... look at historical evidence through many lenses
task: Heavily cited research synthesis on the development of religion, read through many lenses, as a blog series

errors.what: Rewrote research/_homepage/projects.json with json.dump, reformatting the whole file (404/400 line diff)
errors.fix: Reverted; inserted the new theme as a minimal text edit

errors.what: Project README linked reports/ before the report existed; check_md_links failed

integrity_issues: Many standard monographs are cited from bibliographic details, not re-read this session; every notes file tags each claim verified vs bibliographic, and the posts never quote or hang precise figures on unread text.

Notes caught and corrected brief errors: Seshat retake venue (Religion, Brain & Behavior 13(2)), Lightner et al. 2023 title/venue, van Elk 2022's misdescription of Maij et al. 2017, and the 2026 YouGov fraud finding that withdrew the Quiet Revival figures.

doc_friction.issue: PR #9958 moved BASE to /oss-monorepo/ without rewriting READMEs, so main went red; --write then appends a second Live page line and leaves the dead one instead of replacing it.
No theme fits humanities/history research; added a 'humanities' theme for one project (guidance says only when several need it).
#9958 changed BASE but the already-linked regex still matched only monorepo-projects/, failing 6 readme-live-link tests on main; fixed here to accept either base.

After #9958/#9986, 29 venture READMEs whose link label is not 'Live tool' still linked the dead /monorepo-projects/ base and failed this check on main; rewritten in place here. A first attempt rewriting all 1,327 READMEs dragged ~500 venture CI suites in and was reverted.

deviations.why: Added a new homepage theme for a single project: no existing theme (robot societies, scoring, ...) is where a reader would look for history of religion.

'Run the numbers': this is a literature synthesis, not a model; no numbers were invented. A reanalysis of the public Ethnographic Atlas EA034 / Pulotu / Seshat data inventoried in notes 05 is the natural next step.

Widened the PR with base-branch fixes for PR #9958 fallout (research README links rewritten in place; venture_live_links and readme-live-link accept both bases) because main was red on these checks and no fix PR existed.

notes: Eight parallel research strands (48k words of notes), a 10.5k-word synthesis report with 229 linked citations, nine blog posts.
